patch.value: MCP annotation and linked-artifact tools silently read when add is passed at the top level: the strict schema declares add/text but dispatch only hoists ifAbsent

Measured on the feat/write-time-preconditions branch (2026.11.2 source). The strict action schema for comments, notes, learnings and files declares top-level add (and text for comments), so pm_comments {id, add: "x"} validates. The dispatcher's HOISTED_ACTION_OPTION_KEYS hoists only ifAbsent for the annotation actions and nothing for files, so the top-level add never reaches the command. The call becomes a listing read and returns success with count 0. The agent believes it recorded evidence. Only options.add works. Found when pm-gh1576's expected-revision receipt reported expect_hash_unchecked for a comments call that was meant to write. Same class as pm-upi0 (nested unknown keys no-op) and pm-yp56 (comment invocation recording nothing exited 0), but on DECLARED top-level keys, so no unknown-key warning fires.

Every top-level parameter the strict MCP/SDK action schema declares for comments, notes, learnings, files and docs is either hoisted into the command options or removed from the schema, proven by a parity test that iterates the schema-declared keys rather than a hand list; A pm_comments/pm_files call with top-level add writes the entry (or refuses), never returns a listing; Regression test drives the MCP handleRequest path for each annotation action
A declared top-level add on an annotation or linked-artifact MCP tool writes the entry, exactly like options.add
pm_comments {id, add} and pm_files {id, add} return a successful listing with count 0 and write nothing
